basics.name: Parastoo Pilevar
basics.summary: Ph.D. student in ECE at UMD working on efficient and robust deep learning for VLMs and VLAs on edge and robotic platforms. Research centers on model quantization, OOD robustness, and accuracy–memory–latency trade-offs for deployment-constrained perception.

work.company: University of Maryland, College Park — CASE Lab
work.summary: Research on efficient and robust deep learning for VLMs and VLAs on edge platforms.
highlights: Designed systematic PTQ experiments across VLM architectures studying calibration-data sensitivity
Implemented feature-space rectification (Recti-Q) with frozen-backbone LoRA for OOD-robust quantized perception
Built PTQ evaluation pipelines tracking accuracy, memory, and latency across 4-bit and 8-bit configurations

work.company: University of Tehran — Communication Networks Research Group
work.summary: Research on federated learning for edge network optimization.
highlights: Designed cache-replacement policies for edge networks using federated RL and multi-armed bandit frameworks
Investigated privacy-preserving learning strategies in distributed multi-agent systems

publications.name: Recti-Q: Feature-Space Rectification for OOD-Robust Quantized Perception in Edge Robotics
publications.summary: H. Yaghoubi*, P. Pilevar*, M. Lin (*equal contribution). Identifies and quantifies the OOD robustness gap introduced by 4-bit PTQ in large vision backbones on resource-constrained robotic platforms, and proposes a frozen-backbone LoRA adapter that preserves PTQ memory savings while closing most of the robustness gap.

teaching.description: Led discussion sections, wrote and graded problem sets, held office hours for undergraduate engineering students.
